headline: CRA obligations and CBAM ruling tighten compliance for manufacturers

summary.text: Reports say Cyber Resilience Act reporting duties now apply to makers of connected machines, requiring incident-reporting and vulnerability-handling processes before EU sales.
The CRA also reaches software supply chains, so manufacturers must document supplier software and how vulnerabilities are handled.
A proposal to slim down the CRA for mid-sized firms could cut compliance cost, but the final scope is still open.
The EU High Court upheld CBAM as a climate measure, not a tax, so reporting and certificate duties stay, and ETS/CBAM reform will change carbon costs for exporters.

Industrial AI is moving into practice: ORAFOL halved inspection times with AI machine vision, ABB launched an AI Robot Trainer for robot vision programming, and Siemens frames industrial AI as its growth driver.

actions.text: Have product and IT leads check whether your connected machines fall under CRA reporting duties, and set up incident-reporting and vulnerability-handling processes now.
Start listing software components from suppliers in your machines, and keep working on the CRA documentation rather than waiting for a possible relief for mid-sized firms.
Check your CBAM and carbon-cost exposure, including imported covered goods and data needs. Also consider a small AI vision inspection pilot, using the ORAFOL case as a benchmark.
